page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The dedicated CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and is supported by a 33 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25%, indicating weaker single-threaded execution speeds. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks is strong, placing in the top 25% at 192.72 GB/sec, whereas small-block cached reads and large-block writes remain average.

Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps. In application-level benchmarks, the instance delivers average throughput for Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation. Large language model prompt processing for small and medium models is average, though text generation speeds are weak. Given its balanced resource density and average multi-core performance, the m5.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that scale horizontally across many cores rather than relying on high single-thread performance. It is suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded database operations, web serving, and enterprise applications.
